text:
maria: Heads-up — we're planning to enable the new FIPS TLS profile and rotate the KMS wrapping keys across EU/APAC tomorrow 02:00 UTC. Concern: 0-RTT (early_data) session resumption PSKs will be invalidated during rotation and might allow replay or unexpected session failures. Anyone seen staging behavior for early_data with our multi-region PSK rollout?
ryan: Noted. We saw session-resumption churn last week when the rotator rolled a subset of nodes. Hard to tell if it was replay or just failed resume.
sam: Are we changing RBAC for the KMS roles as part of the key prune? That caused unwrap DENY previously and pulled endpoints into fallback.
maria: Yes — least-privilege prune. That's why I'm worried: if unwraps are rejected while clients still try 0-RTT, we may leak inconsistent state or cause silent replays.
tina: Quick Q: can we detect "early_data" attempts in audit logs today? I think TLS layers emit an event but we don't index that field in splunk/dashboard.
sec-oncall: We currently log session resume success/fail and cipher, but not a discrete early_data flag. We can add a parser rule: look for "SSL early_data" entries from edge-proxy and gRPC egress.
infra-bot: rotator-job v3 scheduled: windows=[eu-west1,eu-north1,ap-south1] start=2026-03-23T02:00Z steps=double-wrap->switch->garbage-collect. ETA 2h.
ryan: Double-wrap helps — keep old encryption key available for unwrap during a window, then retire. But PSK-based 0-RTT uses ticket keys stored locally; key rotation must coordinate ticket key lifetime too.
maria: Action item: for the rollout window, disable 0-RTT acceptance at the edge for sessions that rely on ticket keys generated before rotation. How do we implement that quickly?
sam: We can push a config toggle to edge-proxy: "accept_early_data": false. It's a hot config on all LB HA pairs. But must be synchronized regionally — partial disable causes weird latency.
tina: Also need to update audit pipeline: emit an event for any early_data attempt during the window with fields [client_ip, ticket_age, region, cert_chain_id, unwrap_status]. I can drop a parsing rule.
sec-oncall: Recommend runbook step: 1) set accept_early_data=false globally, 2) initiate KMS double-wrap rotation, 3) monitor resume_fail, unwrap_denies, and 0rtt_attempt logs, 4) after rotation, re-enable early_data. Rolling back is re-enable=false.
ryan: Can we avoid full disable by shortening ticket lifetime pre-roll? Force clients to rehandshake. But mobile clients might still rely on tickets.
maria: Good point. Let's do a hybrid: set ticket_max_age=60s on frontends 10m before rotation, then flip accept_early_data=false at start. That reduces surface area and gives clients time to rehandshake.
sam: RBAC change note: ensure the rotator role for unwrap includes a "test-unwind" permission so we can validate unwraps without full production perms. Otherwise we'll hit deny and alarms.
tina: I'll create the parsing rule and dashboard panels: early_data_attempts, ticket_age_distribution, unwrap_deny_rate per region.
infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-3219 with checklist and pre-roll certs.
maria: Ok. Who can own the run during the window? Need someone for 02:00-04:00 UTC.
sec-oncall: I can be primary with ryan backup. I'll prepare the rollback note.
ryan: I'll prep a quick script to toggle accept_early_data across global LB fleet and to set ticket_max_age. Pushing to canary in us-west first.
sam: I'll coordinate the RBAC shadow rollout and confirm KMS policy test-unwrap permits.
tina: Dashboards assembled, will post links once available.
maria: Perfect. Post-mortem checklist: capture all early_data attempts, timestamps of RBAC policy binds, KMS response error codes, and any downstream service retries.
sec-oncall: We'll also add a short alert: if unwrap_denies spike > 0.5% for 5m during rotation, auto-pause the rotator.
maria: Great. Thanks all. I'll send an incident-channel ping pre-roll and include these runbook steps. :white_check_mark:
